name: Wrist Roller
summary: A forearm and grip isolation exercise performed by winding and unwinding a weighted cord around a dowel or roller implement.

setup: Attach a weight plate securely to the end of the wrist roller cord.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding the roller dowel with both hands in a shoulder-width pronated grip.
Extend your arms straight forward at shoulder height, allowing the weight to hang freely near the floor.
steps: Alternate rolling each wrist upward, winding the cord onto the bar until the weight reaches the top.
Reverse the motion under complete control, unwinding the cord one wrist rotation at a time until the plate returns to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and evenly throughout the continuous rolling motion.
cues: Keep your arms locked straight out.
Isolate the motion to your wrists rather than swinging your body.
Control the descent; do not let the cord free-fall.

common_faults.fault: Letting the elbows bend and collapse toward the torso.
common_faults.correction: Maintain straight arms extended forward throughout the set, or rest the roller across rack pins if shoulder fatigue limits forearm training.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the weight to rapidly spin downward uncontrolled.
common_faults.correction: Actively brake and unwind each revolution alternately with both hands.

precautions: Ensure the cord is tightly knotted and verified secure before lifting the weight off the floor.
